scenes.heading: Service Credentials & OAuth Server-to-Server (Part 1 of 2)
scenes.narration: Authentication. Service Credentials & OAuth Server-to-Server (Part 1 of 2). In this video we review 7 key concepts you need to know for the certification.

scenes.question: What is the current standard mechanism for obtaining production access tokens to AEMaaCS?
scenes.heading: OAuth Server-to-Server (S2S) — the current, and only, supported method for production programmatic access
scenes.body: OAuth Server-to-Server (S2S) is the current standard for production-grade programmatic access to AEMaaCS. It replaced the older JWT-based Service Credentials flow, which Adobe fully deprecated.

scenes.question: What is the exact deprecation timeline for JWT-based Service Credentials in Adobe Developer Console?
scenes.heading: New JWT credentials could not be created after June 3, 2024, and all existing JWT credentials stopped working by June 30, 2025
scenes.body: Adobe stopped allowing new JWT (Service Account) credentials to be created on or after June 3, 2024. Every existing JWT credential stopped functioning on or after June 30, 2025 — so any integration still built on JWT is broken today.

scenes.question: Who creates an OAuth Server-to-Server credential, and what is it tied to?
scenes.heading: An Adobe IMS Org Administrator, tied to a Technical Account
scenes.body: An Adobe IMS Org Administrator creates the OAuth Server-to-Server credential — via the AEM Developer Console or Adobe Developer Console — tied to a Technical Account, the identity the credential will authenticate as.

scenes.question: What does an OAuth Server-to-Server credential JSON payload contain?
scenes.heading: A client ID, a client secret, and a set of scopes — no private key and no JWT to build or sign
scenes.body: An OAuth Server-to-Server credential is a JSON payload containing a client ID, a client secret, and the scopes it's allowed to request. Unlike the old JWT flow, there's no private key to manage and no JWT to construct or sign.

scenes.question: How do you exchange OAuth Server-to-Server credentials for an access token?
scenes.heading: A single POST request with grant_type=client_credentials, client_id, client_secret, and scope — no signing step
scenes.body: You make one POST request to https://ims-na1.adobelogin.com/ims/token/v3 with form-encoded parameters grant_type=client_credentials, client_id, client_secret, and scope. The response is an access token — no JWT construction or signing is involved, which is the main simplification over the old flow.

scenes.question: How is the OAuth Server-to-Server access token used once obtained?
scenes.heading: As a Bearer token in the Authorization header, the same way a Local Development Access Token is used
scenes.body: The access token returned by the OAuth Server-to-Server exchange is used exactly like a Local Development Access Token: as a Bearer token in the Authorization header of requests made to AEM's APIs.

scenes.question: How do Service Credentials relate to a Technical Account?
scenes.heading: Tied to a Technical Account; multiple Service Credentials can be active for one Technical Account
scenes.body: Service Credentials are tied to Technical Accounts, and a single Technical Account can have multiple active Service Credentials at once — each one a separate set of client ID/secret pairs authenticating as that same account.
